config.title: Build a modal with escape and backdrop close

intro.title: Build a modal with escape and backdrop close
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a modal (pop-up dialog) that appears on a webpage. You will learn how to close the modal in two user-friendly ways: by pressing the Escape key on the keyboard and by clicking on the backdrop (the dimmed background area). The core programming concept involves handling DOM events to respond to user interactions. You will use fundamental JavaScript constructs like event listeners and state management to control the modal's visibility. This exercise will help you create more interactive and accessible web components.
intro.usecase: Modal dialogs with escape and backdrop closing are essential UI patterns found in nearly every modern web application. You'll encounter them in e-commerce sites when adding items to cart, in banking apps for confirming transactions, and in social media platforms when uploading photos or editing profiles. As a developer, you'll implement these modals for user authentication forms, confirmation dialogs before deleting data, and settings panels in admin dashboards. This pattern improves user experience by providing clear exit paths while keeping users focused on the current task.

objectives: Construct a modal component with open/close state management
Implement event listeners for keyboard interactions
Configure backdrop click functionality to close the modal
Bind escape key press to trigger modal closure
Integrate modal visibility control with user interface elements
Manipulate DOM elements to display and hide modal content
Initialize modal state and event handlers on component mount

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' module.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to use React components and state management.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' module.

steps.title: Create the Modal component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Modal that returns null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. The component should be named Modal and return null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Modal component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Modal component is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: A functional component named Modal is created and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the Modal component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named Modal and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a functional component named Modal that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize modal state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the Modal component, use useState to create an 'isOpen' state variable and setter, initialized to false.
steps.hint: Call useState with false as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into two variables (e.g., isOpen and setIsOpen).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a boolean state variable
const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The Modal component will have an isOpen state variable (initially false) and a setIsOpen setter function.
successCriteria: The Modal component contains a useState call that initializes isOpen to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with false as the initial value inside the Modal component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Use useState(false) inside the Modal component.

steps.title: Define openModal handler
steps.instruction: Inside the Modal component, define a function named openModal that sets the isOpen state to true.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setIsOpen with the value true.
steps.expectedOutcome: The openModal function is defined and ready to be called to open the modal.
successCriteria: The openModal function is defined and calls setIsOpen(true).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure openModal is a function that calls setIsOpen with true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The openModal handler isn't defined correctly. It should be a function that sets isOpen to true.

steps.title: Define closeModal handler
steps.instruction: In your Modal component, define a function named closeModal that sets the isOpen state to false.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setIsOpen with the value false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The closeModal function is defined and ready to be used to close the modal.
successCriteria: A function named closeModal is defined that calls setIsOpen(false).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the closeModal handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named closeModal and sets isOpen to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The closeModal function is not defined correctly. Try creating a function that calls setIsOpen(false).

steps.title: Add conditional rendering for modal structure
steps.instruction: In your Modal component's return statement, add conditional rendering that returns JSX for a modal backdrop and content when isOpen is true, otherwise returns null.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator (isOpen ? ... : null) to conditionally render the modal structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Modal component now conditionally renders modal content based on the isOpen state.
successCriteria: Modal component returns JSX with a ternary operator checking isOpen, rendering modal structure when true and null when false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using a ternary operator (isOpen ? ... : null) in the return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering isn't quite right. Check that you're using isOpen in a ternary operator to return JSX when true and null when false.

steps.title: Add modal content and backdrop click handler
steps.instruction: Inside the conditional JSX, add a backdrop div that covers the screen and a modal content div with some text. Wire the backdrop div's onClick to call the closeModal handler.
steps.hint: Add a div with a semi-transparent background that fills the viewport, and inside it add another div for the modal content. Use onClick on the backdrop div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The modal will show a backdrop and content when isOpen is true, and clicking the backdrop will close the modal.
successCriteria: The JSX includes a backdrop div with onClick={closeModal} and a modal content div with some text inside.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both the backdrop div (with onClick) and the modal content div inside the conditional return.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction: you need to add a backdrop div with onClick={closeModal} and a modal content div inside the conditional JSX.

steps.title: Add escape key handler with useEffect
steps.instruction: Import useEffect from 'react' and add it to your Modal component to handle the Escape key press for closing the modal.
steps.hint: Use useEffect to add an event listener for the 'keydown' event. Inside the event handler, check if the pressed key is 'Escape' and call closeModal. Remember to return a cleanup function that removes the event listener.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Modal component will now listen for the Escape key press and close the modal when Escape is pressed, with proper cleanup of the event listener.
successCriteria: useEffect is imported from 'react' and implemented in the Modal component with an event listener for 'keydown' that checks for 'Escape' key and calls closeModal, including a cleanup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported useEffect, added the event listener for 'keydown', checked for the 'Escape' key, and included a cleanup function to remove the listener.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Escape key handler is not yet implemented correctly. Check that you've imported useEffect, added the event listener, and included proper cleanup.

steps.title: Add open button and wire click
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the Modal component's return statement, before the conditional modal rendering, with an onClick handler that calls openModal.
steps.hint: Place the button outside the conditional return, so it's always visible. Use the onClick prop and pass openModal as the handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button appears on the page and clicking it opens the modal by setting isOpen to true.
successCriteria: A button element with onClick={openModal} is added inside the Modal component's return statement, before the conditional modal rendering.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it's placed before the conditional return and has onClick={openModal}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not correctly wired. Add a button with onClick={openModal} inside the return statement.

steps.title: Add close button inside modal
steps.instruction: Inside the modal content div, add a button element with text 'Close' and wire its onClick to the closeModal handler.
steps.hint: Place the button inside the modal content div. Use onClick={closeModal} to call the handler when clicked.
steps.expectedOutcome: The modal will include a close button that, when clicked, triggers the closeModal handler to hide the modal.
successCriteria: A button with text 'Close' is present inside the modal content div, and its onClick is set to closeModal.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but check that it's inside the modal content div and its onClick is correctly wired to closeModal.
steps.feedbackWrong: The close button is missing or not properly wired. Add a button with onClick={closeModal} inside the modal content div.
